steps.text: Spread a thin layer of barbecue sauce on the bottom of a slow cooker. Alternately layer pork chops with barbecue sauce. Pour any remaining sauce over the final layer of chops.
Cook on Low for 6 hours or High for 3 to 4 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker BBQ Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Learn how to cook pork chops in a crock pot with this super easy, two-ingredient slow cooker recipe for pork BBQ steaks made with store-bought sauce.

video.description: Pork chops covered in sweet and savory barbeque sauce is all you need for this meal! Place in a slow cooker while you make your sides! Mashed potatoes and green beans are the perfect side dishes to round out this dinner.

review.reviewBody: This was only the 2nd thing that I've tried cooking in a slow cooker and it came out so delicious! I did add about 1/4 cup of water to the bottom to avoid burning and I added onion slices on top of each pork chop as I was layering. The result was incredible, no knife required, and the slightly thinned onion loaded sauce was good on my potatoes. I'm going to try the leftovers over rice.

This is a good basic recipe. My family really enjoyed the Zesty Slow Cooker Chicken BBQ recipe by Zanne Peters from this website which had these additional ingredients: 1/2 cup of italian dressing, 1/4 cup brown sugar, and 2 tbsp. of worcestershire sauce. If you want to add a little kick to this recipe, I would suggest adding these along with the BBQ sauce of your choice. It gives it a great taste whether you're using chicken or pork!! Thanks!

I've been making something similar for years. I put down a layer of 1/3" sliced carrots on the bottom of the crock. Salt and pepper 5-6 chops, arrange overlapping around the crock. Cut 2 medium onions into 6 wedges each and sandwich them between the chops and along the sides to help separate and prop up chops. No water needed, onions produce enough liquid. Add minced garlic to taste (1 Tbs). Use only 1/3 - 1/2 bottle of Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce on top. Always cooked on low. Once done, remove chops and vegetables and thicken liquid with a cornstarch and water mix. Makes an excellent gravy

I changed the servings to make it enough for just my SO and I by cutting it down to just 3 chops. I first marinated the pork chops overnight in a marinade that consisted of olive oil, soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, steakhouse pepper, Lawry's seasoning salt, fresh minced garlic and 1/3 cup of Strongbow hard cider. The next day when I was ready to cook my chops I first pan-seared them on all sides (for about 3-4 minutes on each side) in some olive oil, and for the last 3 minutes I added in some unsalted butter for the last bit of browning. I then added in a thin layer of water to the bottom of my crockpot before adding in my chops. I covered the chops with my favorite BBQ sauce (Stubb's Sweet Heat) and then added in some slices of onion on top. The last thing I did was smash a clove of garlic and toss it in before covering and setting on low and cooking for 8 hours.

Loved the recipe with modifications. I combined 1/2 cup water with 1/2 cup BBQ sauce. Poured it into the bottom of the crockpot. I seasoned both sides of the pork chops with onion powder and garlic powder. Placed pork chops in crockpot. Combined 1/2 BBQ sauce, 1/4 cup brown sugar and 2 TBS soy sauce. Poured this over pork chops. Cooked on low for 6 hours. Meat was delicious, moist and fell off the bone.

As a 53yr old bachelor, learning to try and cook things has been rather difficult. This was very easy! I got 6 (it called for 8, but it’s just me), and I did everything it called for. I did however add some sea salt and pepper (very little of both), and a very small amount of brown sugar, just to sweeten up some. I did these, mashed potatoes, and some baked beans (store deli prepared beans), set timer for about 4 1/2hrs. I did add just alittle bit of Coke per a family secret, and the meat was absolutely amazing. The cut with a plastic fork. It made the home smell so good too. Thanks for the help!

Very easy recipe. I had 6 bone in pork chops average in thickness. I used another reviewer's idea of mixing 1/2 c bbq sauce with liquid on bottom. I used Dr Pepper. I seasoned the chops with garlic pepper and layered onion on bottom and between the chops. They cooked for 6 hours on low. The chops were very tender. The sauce was thin so I may thicken it up next time. As it was I just spooned some sauce on the chops as I plated them. Served with potato wedges.

I tweaked this recipe to give it a taste of Jamaica and Japan. I made 1 pork chop bone in just over 1lb and I cooked it on low for about 4 hours. It had an nice gravy. 
Season the chop with granulated onion and garlic powder, black pepper. 
Rub a pinch of oil on the chop. Place it in the slow cooker. 
Mix 2 tsps of Walkers Wood Jerk Sauce with 2TBS low sodium Tamari (or soy) sauce and 2 tsp mirin, and juice of half a small lime. 
Add 1 thumb size of ginger smashed. Stir well. 
Slice half small onion and one stalk of green onion. 
Pour the sauce mix on top of the chop and flip it once to coat both sides. Add the onion and scallion/green onion. 

Serve with steaming hot rice.

Loved it, just like another reviewer I chopped up one onion and layered it in between the chops and BBQ sauce. In 1 hour on high (since the chops I used were thin) they were done. I put the chops on brown rice and had a veg medley on the side. 

It was tasty, may end up putting chunks of pineapple in it next time to see how it dose. Its a good base to work off of. =D

This recipe has been around for decades, but it’s still very good! I’d be careful adding onion, however, because onions release a Lot of liquid while cooking and will thin the BBQ sauce dramatically. Dried onion flakes or onion powder would work better in this. Also, it doesn’t need added liquid, unless people want to add the flavor of broth, Coke, or Dr. Pepper—it’s easy enough to thicken with a little corn starch mixed in water and allowed to thicken in the pot at the last part of cooking.

Pork chops are always hit or miss with my husband but these were definitely a hit. I changed the recipe a bit, but did not add water like most had suggested. I coated the bottom of my slow cooker with a little EVOO and seasoned the pork chops with kosher salt, pepper, smoked paprika and garlic powder. I thinly sliced some yellow onion and put them at the bottom of the slow cooker, and around the meat. I used Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce and added some garlic salt and about 1-2 TBSP of mesquite liquid smoke. I cooked them 2 hours on low and then 2 hours on high. I kept checking on the meat to make sure it was not too dry but that it fell apart easily. They came out very good. I paired it with some baked mac & cheese. Easy weeknight meal that I will definitely make again.

This could not have been easier. I used boneless pork chops since that is what I had. It was almost like having shredded pulled pork for two. I had them with Mac and Cheese and mashed carrots. It was meant to be the perfect meal. Unfortunately I planned it for a work day, which exceeded the 6 hours on low so they were not as moist and juicy as we would have liked. I usually have better luck in other slow cooker, pork chops recipes but not with this one. I tend to think that even 6 hours might be too long, but then again I only cooked two!
Very easy recipe, though the chops were a tad dry and kind of bland.
I didn't change a thing. So delicious and easy to make. I serve it with basmati rice and drizzle the sauce over it. My husband likes a little kick to it so we use Sweet Heat BBQ Sauce.
Cooked six pork chops on low for 4.5 hours and they were overcooked. Will try for three hours next time.
The sauce flavor was flat after 6 hrs of cookin,have some fresh sauce for serving.
Ace this weekend with I” pork chops, dry and tasteless. ☹️
Fabulous
Easy and tender and delicious
Awesome 👍
